label: Step 2 (third original token) when the first token is 1/m/h/x/n/v
explanation: Fires almost only at t=2, the third original-phase input, and only when the sequence started with one of a small set of first tokens. First token 1 gives the largest activations: the top examples all begin 1 3, and 1 carries about 32% of the mass. m, h and x give strong activations, about 20% of the mass each. n and v give weaker ones, about 5% each. First token u gives faint activations and s rarely fires. Silent at t=0,1 and at t>=3 (apart from a handful of t=3/5 cases), at the delimiter, and during the copy phase. The current input token at t=2 has almost no effect (about 1.1-1.2x lift for every token). Dev F1 0.93, mass recall 0.99. The misses are small activations on sequences starting with u or s. The false positives are mostly at the n/v boundary.

issues: The core claims check out. The feature fires only at t=2 (95393 of 95499 active steps on dev; 96 at t=3, 10 at t=5, 10 in copy, none at the delimiter). Activation mass by first token: 1=32%, m=20%, h=21%, x=16%, n=5%, v=4.5%. With first token 1, m, h or x, precision at t=2 is 1.0. The current (third) input token gives a flat 1.1-1.2x lift, as claimed.

Systematic gap: the explanation calls the n/v false positives boundary noise, but they depend on the SECOND token (orig(1)). Precision at t=2 for first=v, by second token: a/c/j/n/v = 0.0, s = 0.03, o = 0.50, i/t/w = 0.58-0.61, while b/g/h/l/m/p/r/x/y/z/1/2/3 = 0.96-1.0. For first=n with second in {a,c,j,n,s,v,o}, precision is 0.29.

Same pattern for first=u (which the predicate leaves out). The feature fires reliably when the second token is h (0.93), 1 (0.93) or m (0.80), often for x/3/2/r (0.52-0.69), and almost never for most other second tokens. So the u/s misses are not scattered small activations either: they are a second-token effect.

This suggests the feature responds to a combined score over the first two tokens. The same tokens 1/m/h/x push it on in either position, and a/c/j/n/s/v push it off. A rule based on the first token alone is only an approximation.
Better predicate (handles second-token modulation at the boundary): test F1 0.964 (P 0.971, R 0.958, mass recall 0.996), up from 0.933.
skeptic.revised_label: Step 2 (third original token), gated by the first two tokens: always fires when the first token is 1/m/h/x; when it is n/v/u, fires depending on the second token (on for 1/m/h/x and similar, off for a/c/j/n/s/v)
